reported.title: delete_document performs no admin or ownership check
reported.body: `delete_document` performs no authorization at all: it neither calls `_assert_admin(user)` nor checks ownership via `documents.get_document(doc_id, user)`. It is exposed to every authenticated caller through `handle_delete_document` in `app/__init__.py`, so any logged-in user can permanently delete any other user's document by enumerating `doc_id`. Add an ownership/admin check before the DELETE, e.g. `get_document(doc_id, user)` (which raises `NotFound`/`Forbidden`) or `_assert_admin(user)` depending on the intended semantics.

reported.title: purge_user swallows the admin authorization failure
reported.body: The admin check in `purge_user` is wrapped in `try/except Exception: pass`, so the `Forbidden` raised by `_assert_admin` is discarded and execution continues to the DELETE statements. The authorization check is therefore a no-op: any caller can purge every document belonging to an arbitrary `target_user_id`, destroying data.

reported.title: SECRET_KEY falls back to a hardcoded development value
reported.body: `SECRET_KEY` now falls back to the hardcoded literal "dev-secret-change-me" when `QUORUM_DEMO_SECRET` is unset. This key is the HMAC key used by `auth.sign()`, which backs both session tokens (`auth.verify_session_token`) and share-link signatures (`sharing.resolve_share_link`). Any deployment that forgets the environment variable silently runs with a publicly known key, letting anyone forge `<user_id>.<signature>` tokens for arbitrary users — including admins — and forge share signatures. The previous `os.environ[...]` form failed fast at import time precisely to prevent this.

reported.title: list_documents no longer clamps limit to MAX_PAGE_SIZE
reported.body: The clamp to `Config.MAX_PAGE_SIZE` was removed, so `limit` is now whatever the caller passes and flows straight into `LIMIT ?`. `handle_list_documents` exposes this to any authenticated user, who can request an arbitrarily large page and force the entire `documents` table to be materialised into memory (`db.query` calls `fetchall()` and the result is copied into a list of dicts) — an unpaginated query / resource exhaustion vector. Keep the clamp; if the export UI needs bigger pages, raise `MAX_PAGE_SIZE` instead.

reported.title: Path traversal: export filename joined without validation
reported.body: `export_path` joins the caller-supplied `filename` into the export directory without validation, and `export_document`/`handle_export` pass user input straight through. A filename like `../../../../etc/cron.d/job` — or an absolute path, since `os.path.join` discards the prefix when the second argument is absolute — writes attacker-controlled JSON anywhere the process can write. The repository already provides `validators.export_name()`, which reduces a name to a single safe segment; run `filename` through it (adding `from . import validators`) before joining, or verify the resolved realpath stays under `user_dir` as `indexer.extract_text` does.

reported.title: TOCTOU between existence check and file write in export_document
reported.body: The `os.path.exists` guard is separated from `open(destination, "w")` by an explicit `time.sleep(0.2)`. Anything that creates `destination` during that window — a concurrent export, or an attacker who can create a file or symlink in the export directory — is silently overwritten, since `"w"` truncates. Perform the create-if-absent atomically with the `"x"` mode instead of checking first.

reported.title: Path traversal in write_named_report via unsanitized filename parameter
reported.body: `write_named_report` joins `_user_dir(user)` with an unvalidated `filename` parameter using `os.path.join`. Directory traversal sequences like `../../` allow callers to overwrite arbitrary files on disk.

reported.title: SQL injection: search term interpolated into the query
reported.body: `term` (and `user["id"]`) are interpolated into the SQL text with an f-string and the query is passed to `db.query(sql)` with no parameters. `term` reaches here straight from `handle_search(token, term, ...)`, so a caller can close the quote and append arbitrary SQL — e.g. `x' OR 1=1 --` returns every user's documents, and a UNION payload can dump other tables such as `users`. Bind the values instead; `column` is already constrained by the `SORTABLE` allowlist and may stay interpolated.

reported.title: Mutable default argument accumulates scopes across calls
reported.body: `scopes: list = []` is a mutable default evaluated once at function definition, and `scopes.append("read")` mutates it, so the same list object is shared by every call that omits the argument. When a caller does pass a list, the function mutates the caller's object too, silently widening the scopes of the caller's own data structure. Use `scopes: list = None` and build a fresh list inside the function (`scopes = list(scopes or [])`).

reported.title: Share signature compared with non-constant-time ==
reported.body: The share-link HMAC is compared with `!=`, which short-circuits on the first differing byte and leaks signature bytes through timing — exactly the side channel `auth.verify_session_token` deliberately avoids with `hmac.compare_digest`. Use `if not hmac.compare_digest(expected, signature):` and add `import hmac` at the top of the module.

reported.title: Share links never expire: TTL stored as a duration and never checked
reported.body: `expires_at = (ttl or DEFAULT_TTL_SECONDS)` stores a duration in seconds into the `expires_in` column rather than an absolute expiry timestamp, and `resolve_share_link` selects only `doc_id, scopes` and never compares anything against the current time. A leaked or shared token therefore grants access to the document forever. Store `time.time() + (ttl or DEFAULT_TTL_SECONDS)` and reject rows whose expiry has passed during resolution. `resolve_share_link` additionally ignores the stored `scopes` and returns the full document row regardless of what the share granted.

reported.title: purge_user deletes orphaned shares belonging to all users
reported.body: The cleanup statement `DELETE FROM shares WHERE doc_id NOT IN (SELECT id FROM documents)` is not scoped to the purged user. It deletes every orphaned share row in the table, including rows belonging to unrelated users that were orphaned for other reasons — collateral data loss on every purge. Scope the delete to the documents just removed (capture their ids before the first DELETE and delete shares for those ids only).

reported.title: SSRF: user-supplied URL fetched with no scheme or host allowlist
reported.body: `fetch_remote_document` issues `requests.get(url)` on a URL supplied by the caller (`handle_import_url`) with no scheme or host validation and with redirects followed by default. A caller can point it at `http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/...`, internal `http://localhost:PORT` services, or other non-public hosts, and the whole response body is returned to them in `"body"`. Validate the parsed scheme (http/https only), resolve the host and reject loopback/link-local/private ranges, and disable redirects or re-validate each hop. The body is also read in full via `response.text` with no size cap, an unbounded allocation driven by a remote server.

reported.title: Scope check for document.report always passes (action unregistered)
reported.body: `permissions.has_scope(user, "document.report")` is a no-op: `"document.report"` is not a key in `permissions.REQUIRED_SCOPES` (which lists only `document.read`, `document.share`, `document.delete`, `document.export`), and `has_scope` returns True for any unlisted action — the module docstring warns about exactly this failure mode. `write_report`, reachable by any authenticated user through `handle_write_report`, is therefore effectively unguarded while reading as if protected. Add `"document.report": "documents:write"` to `REQUIRED_SCOPES`.

reported.title: audit.record called with arguments in the wrong order
reported.body: `audit.record` has the signature `record(action, user_id, doc_id, detail="")`. This call passes the `user` dict as `action` and the string `"document.report"` as `user_id`, so `int("document.report")` raises `ValueError`. `write_report` therefore always fails after the report file has already been written, and no audit row is ever recorded for this privileged action.

reported.title: Formatter registry points at modules that do not exist
reported.body: The registered module paths `app.formatters.markdown`, `app.formatters.html` and `app.formatters.pdf` do not exist anywhere in the repository — there is no `app/formatters` package. `available_formats()` (exposed via `handle_available_formats`) advertises three formats, but `load_formatter()` raises `ModuleNotFoundError` for every one of them.

reported.title: TOCTOU between existence check and write, widened by sleep
reported.body: The `os.path.exists` check is separated from `open(destination, "w")` by a deliberate `time.sleep(0.2)`, widening the race window. Between the check and the open, another process — or the same user racing two exports — can create the path, including as a symlink, and the `"w"` open follows it and truncates the target. Use an atomic exclusive create instead of check-then-write.

reported.title: Share signature compared with != instead of constant-time compare
reported.body: `resolve_share_link` verifies the HMAC with `expected != signature`, a short-circuiting comparison, unlike `auth.verify_session_token` which deliberately uses `hmac.compare_digest`. An attacker who can time repeated resolve attempts for a known `doc_id`/`token` can recover a valid signature byte by byte and read the document. Import `hmac` in this module and use `if not hmac.compare_digest(expected, signature or ""):`. Separately, the function returns the entire document row while ignoring `share["scopes"]`, so a read-only share still exposes the full record.

The default list persists across calls, and when a caller does pass a list (as `handle_create_share` forwards) that caller's list is modified in place — state leaks between requests and the returned `scopes` are not what the caller supplied. survived.body: Dropping `min(int(limit), Config.MAX_PAGE_SIZE)` makes the page size fully caller-controlled: `handle_list_documents(token, limit=10**9)` pulls the entire `documents` table into memory in one request — a trivial denial of service for any authenticated user. `Config.MAX_PAGE_SIZE` is now unused. If the export UI needs larger pages, raise `MAX_PAGE_SIZE` rather than removing the bound.

survived.title: Scope check is a no-op: document.report absent from REQUIRED_SCOPES
survived.body: `permissions.has_scope` returns `True` for any action missing from `REQUIRED_SCOPES` (documented explicitly in app/permissions.py), and `"document.report"` is not in that table — it lists only `document.read`, `document.share`, `document.delete`, `document.export`. So this gate always passes and `write_report` (exposed as `handle_write_report`) is unprotected while reading as if it were scope-checked. Add `"document.report": "documents:write"` to `REQUIRED_SCOPES`.

survived.title: audit.record called with arguments in the wrong order
survived.body: `audit.record` is defined as `record(action: str, user_id: int, doc_id: int, detail: str = "")` in app/audit.py, but this call passes the `user` dict as `action` and the string `"document.report"` as `user_id`. `int("document.report")` raises `ValueError`, so every successful report write raises after the file has already been written: the caller sees a failure for a report that exists on disk, and no audit row is recorded.

survived.title: Share links never expire; TTL stored as duration and never checked
survived.body: `expires_at` is assigned a duration (`ttl or DEFAULT_TTL_SECONDS`), not an absolute timestamp, and is written to the `expires_in` column. `resolve_share_link` selects only `doc_id, scopes` and never compares anything against the current time, so every minted share link is valid forever and the `ttl` parameter has no effect. Store an absolute expiry (`time.time() + ttl`) and reject expired rows during resolution.

survived.title: Formatter registry points at modules that do not exist
survived.body: `FORMATTERS` maps to `app.formatters.markdown`, `app.formatters.html`, and `app.formatters.pdf`, but there is no `app/formatters` package in the repository. `available_formats()` (exported as `handle_available_formats`) advertises three formats, and any `load_formatter` call for them raises `ModuleNotFoundError` rather than the documented `ValueError`. Add the modules or register only formats that exist.

reported.title: SQL injection: search term interpolated into query string
reported.body: `search()` builds the SQL with an f-string, interpolating the caller-supplied `term` directly into the statement (`documents_fts MATCH '{term}'`) and passing the finished string to `db.query(sql)` with no parameters. `db.query` (app/db.py:20) hands the string straight to `sqlite3.Connection.execute`, so anything the user types is executed as SQL. A term such as `x' OR 1=1 --` drops the owner scoping and returns every user's documents. Reachable from `handle_search` in `app/__init__.py` by any authenticated user. Bind `term` (and `user["id"]`, `limit`) as parameters; only `column`, which comes from the `SORTABLE` allowlist, may be interpolated.

reported.title: Path traversal: export filename joined without validation
reported.body: `export_path` joins the caller-supplied `filename` onto the export directory with no validation. The repo already has `validators.export_name` (strips directory parts, rejects dotfiles and traversal, enforces a single-segment allowlist) and `reports.write_report` uses it, but `export_document` — reachable via `handle_export` in `app/__init__.py` — does not. A filename of `../../../../etc/cron.d/x`, or an absolute path (which `os.path.join` honours, discarding the prefix), lets an authenticated user write attacker-controlled JSON anywhere the process can write. Pass `filename` through `validators.export_name()` before joining.

reported.title: TOCTOU between existence check and export file write
reported.body: `export_document` checks `os.path.exists(destination)`, then deliberately sleeps 200 ms, then opens the path with mode `"w"`. Anything created at that path during the sleep window — a symlink planted by another local user, or a concurrent export of the same name — is silently followed and truncated, defeating the existence check. Create the file atomically instead: `open(destination, "x", encoding="utf-8")` (or `os.open` with `O_CREAT|O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW`) and drop the sleep between the check and the write.

reported.title: Share signature compared with == instead of constant time
reported.body: `resolve_share_link` compares the recomputed HMAC against the client-supplied `signature` using `!=`, which short-circuits on the first differing byte. Everywhere else in this codebase the comparison is constant-time (`auth.verify_session_token` uses `hmac.compare_digest`). The attacker controls both `doc_id` and `token` and can repeat the call freely, so the timing side channel allows recovering a valid signature byte by byte. Import `hmac` in this module and use `if not hmac.compare_digest(expected, signature):`.

reported.title: Mutable default argument for scopes is mutated and returned
reported.body: `scopes: list = []` is a mutable default evaluated once at import time, and the function mutates it (`scopes.append("read")`) and then returns that same object in the result dict (`"scopes": scopes`). All default-argument calls share one list, so any caller that mutates the returned list — or any future code path appending another scope — permanently alters the default, and later share links silently inherit scopes they were never granted. Use `None` as the default and copy the caller's list.

reported.title: Expiration check missing when resolving share links
reported.body: `resolve_share_link` does not verify if the share link has passed its expiry timestamp (`expires_in`), allowing expired share tokens to remain valid indefinitely.

reported.title: SSRF: user-supplied URL fetched with no scheme/host allowlist
reported.body: `fetch_remote_document` issues `requests.get(url, ...)` on a URL supplied verbatim by the caller (`handle_import_url`), with no scheme or host allowlist and with redirects followed by default. An authenticated user can point the import at `http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/...` or a loopback/private-network admin port, and the response body is handed back to them in the `body` field. Validate the parsed scheme against http/https, resolve the host and reject loopback/link-local/private addresses, and disable or re-validate redirects. Additionally, `response.text` reads the whole body with no size cap, an unbounded allocation driven by a remote server.

reported.title: HMAC signing key falls back to a hardcoded default
reported.body: `SECRET_KEY` now silently falls back to the hardcoded value `"dev-secret-change-me"` when `QUORUM_DEMO_SECRET` is unset. That key is the HMAC key used by `auth.sign`, which authenticates session tokens (`auth.verify_session_token` accepts `<user_id>.<signature>`) and share-link signatures. A deployment that forgets the environment variable no longer fails fast at import; it runs with a publicly known key, so anyone can forge a session token for an arbitrary user id, including an admin. Restore the fail-fast `os.environ[...]` lookup and put any test-only default in the test harness.

reported.title: delete_document performs no ownership or admin check
reported.body: `delete_document` performs no authorization at all: it neither calls `_assert_admin` nor checks that `doc_id` belongs to `user` (contrast `documents.get_document`, which enforces `owner_id == user["id"] or is_admin`). It is exported through `handle_delete_document` in `app/__init__.py`, so any authenticated user can delete any other user's document by guessing an id, and the log line then falsely attributes an authorized deletion. Add `get_document(doc_id, user)` before the DELETE, or scope the statement with `AND owner_id = ?`.

reported.title: Admin check in purge_user swallowed by bare except
reported.body: The admin check in `purge_user` is wrapped in `try: ... except Exception: pass`, which swallows the `Forbidden` raised by `_assert_admin`. Execution then continues and deletes every document owned by `target_user_id` for any caller. A failed authorization check here is indistinguishable from a passed one. Remove the try/except so `_assert_admin(user)` propagates. Separately, `DELETE FROM shares WHERE doc_id NOT IN (SELECT id FROM documents)` is unscoped and removes orphaned share rows belonging to unrelated users.

reported.title: Scope check for document.report always passes
reported.body: `permissions.has_scope(user, "document.report")` is a no-op guard: `"document.report"` is not a key in `REQUIRED_SCOPES` (app/permissions.py:10-15), and `has_scope` returns `True` for any action absent from that table — as the module docstring warns in capitals. `write_report`, exposed via `handle_write_report`, therefore runs for every authenticated user regardless of granted scopes, while reading like an enforced check.
